children: Aris Mining Corporation (Aris Mining or the Company) reports gold production of 217.3 thousand ounces (koz) for the nine months ended September 30, 2026 (YTD 2026), up 16% from YTD 2025. Based on year-to-date operating performance and the outlook for the fourth quarter, the Company remains on track to meet the lower end of 2026 production guidance of 300,000 to 350,000 ounces. All amounts are in U.S. dollars unless otherwise indicated.
Neil Woodyer, Chair and CEO, commented “During the third quarter, we continued to advance our growth plans at both Segovia and Marmato.

At Segovia, owner-mined tonnes increased approximately 23% from Q1 to Q3. Production from our external mining partners was affected earlier in the year by temporary constraints on access to explosives, which impacted their tonnes and grades. This issue was resolved in September under the new Colombian administration, positioning partner production to increase toward planned ramp-up levels.

At Marmato, the new Cascabel 3 filtered tailings facility, a key component of the expansion project, has been commissioned. We used the associated planned downtime to carry out upgrades at the existing flotation plant, while construction of the new CIP plant continues to advance toward first gold in Q4.

With mining underway in the Bulk Mining Zone, ore stockpiles building ahead of CIP commissioning, and the Cascabel 3 filtered tailing facility now operational, Marmato is well positioned heading into 2027. Together, the Segovia and Marmato expansions are expected to support annual gold production of approximately 500,000 ounces once fully ramped-up.”
Q3 2026 production of 69.3 koz, resulting in YTD 2026 production of 217.3 koz, up 16% from the same period in 2025.

Q3 2026 gold sales of 68.4 koz at an average realized price of approximately $4,204 per ounce, resulting in Q3 2026 gold revenue of approximately $287 million and over $972 million on a year-to-date basis.

The Marmato expansion project achieved another key milestone with the commissioning of the new Cascabel 3 filtered tailings facility. The planned transition from Cascabel 2 required approximately four weeks of flotation plant downtime, which was used to complete upgrades and extensive maintenance and contributed to lower production in Q3 2026.
The refurbishment of the primary ball mill and the installation of a new regrind mill and Knelson concentrator have increased the Marmato flotation plant's capacity to 1,250 tonnes per day (tpd).
Marmato’s 5,000 tpd CIP plant remains on track for first gold in Q4 2026.
Cash balance of $419 million at September 30, 2026, including $42 million from the third and final Marmato construction funding instalment from Wheaton Precious Metals.
The Toroparu Prefeasibility Study remains on track for completion in Q4 2026.
At Soto Norte, the technical mine plan has been approved by the ANM and preparation of the Environmental and Social Impact Assessment has been completed for community engagement.
The Company expects to report its full Q3 2026 financial and operating results on or around November 4, 2026.

Aris Mining is a Canadian gold mining company focused on South America. The Company operates the Segovia and Marmato underground gold mines in Colombia, which together produced approximately 257,000 ounces of gold in 2025. Aris Mining is listed on the Toronto Stock Exchange and the New York Stock Exchange under the symbol ARIS.

The Company is advancing expansion projects at Segovia and Marmato that are expected to increase annual gold production to 500,000 ounces2, driven by the ramp-up at Segovia following the installation of the second mill which was completed in June 2025, and construction of the new Marmato bulk mine and CIP plant, with first gold expected in Q4 2026.

Aris Mining’s portfolio supports a longer-term objective of approximately 1 million ounces of annual gold production3. Key projects include the high-grade Soto Norte gold project in Colombia, where preparation of the Environmental and Social Impact Assessment (ESIA) has been completed for community engagement, and the Toroparu gold project in Guyana, where a Prefeasibility Study is in progress and a construction decision is expected in early 2027.
Additional information on Aris Mining can be found at www.aris-mining.com, www.sedarplus.ca, and on www.sec.gov.

3 Includes potential production estimates from Toroparu, which is based on a preliminary economic assessment effective October 21, 2025, which contemplates a 7.0 Mtpa operation over a 21.3-year mine life with average annual gold production of approximately 235 koz at a base case gold price of US$3,000/oz. The preliminary economic assessment is preliminary in nature and includes inferred mineral resources that are considered too speculative geologically to have the economic considerations applied to them that would enable them to be categorized as mineral reserves, and there is no certainty that the preliminary economic assessment will be realized. Mineral resources that are not mineral reserves do not have demonstrated economic viability. There can be no assurance that the projected production will be achieved. Such production also remains subject to obtaining all necessary permits and to formal construction decisions by the Company, in each case for both Soto Norte and Toroparu.
